title: Scientists Put Zebra Coats on Horses to Solve a Mystery
subject: zebra

scenes.text: For over a century, scientists argued about why zebras have stripes. Then they put zebra coats on horses.
The suspect was a fly: the biting horsefly.
Researchers watched flies around zebras and horses. Flies landed on zebras less than a quarter as often.
They still came close. But near stripes, they didn't slow down to land. They crashed into the zebra and bounced off.
And horses wearing striped coats? Far fewer flies landed on the coat than on their bare heads.
The stripes don't repel flies. They wreck their landing.

description:
For over a century, scientists argued about why zebras have stripes.
A study with striped coats on horses found biting flies land on zebras less than a quarter as often as on horses, because stripes ruin their landing.
What animal feature should science explain next?
first_comment: The study came from researchers at UC Davis and the University of Bristol in 2019. Do you think this settles the old debate?
